#### 1. Tessadori-van Haaften neurodevelopmental syndrome 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.420)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8936459, Reactome:R-HSA-8939236)

**Proposed mechanism:** GATA1 pathogenic variant (LOVD_GATA1) —DISRUPTS→ GATA1 (HGNC:4005); GATA1 (HGNC:4005) —DECREASES→ Hematopoietic stem cell differentiation (GO:0030097); Hematopoietic stem cell differentiation (GO:0030097) —LEADS_TO→ Transient myeloproliferative syndrome (MONDO:0008040); GATA1 (HGNC:4005) —DECREASES→ Neuronal development and differentiation (GO:0048666); Neuronal development and differentiation (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Tessadori-van Haaften neurodevelopmental syndrome 2 (MONDO:0030730). Pathogenic variants in GATA1 lead to haploinsufficiency in hematopoietic stem cells, disrupting normal differentiation and causing transient myeloproliferative syndrome. A similar, potentially more severe loss-of-function in GATA1 affects neuronal development pathways, leading to Tessadori-van Haaften neurodevelopmental syndrome 2.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in GATA1 in individuals diagnosed with either transient myeloproliferative syndrome or Tessadori-van Haaften neurodevelopmental syndrome 2, or identification of distinct genes with no functional overlap that fully explain both phenotypes. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing pathogenic variants in GATA1 with frequencies significantly higher than expected for rare alleles in both hematopoietic and neurological disease cohorts.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GATA1 in both hematopoietic and neuronal development could reveal common therapeutic targets or strategies for managing overlapping aspects of these distinct developmental disorders. It highlights the pleiotropic nature of transcription factors and their critical, context-dependent roles in different cell types.
